templates.current:
**{total} projects, of which {baseline} are user-reference projects and {added} were added in this round.** Feature verification: {reviewed}; metrics snapshot: `{as_of}` (UTC).

Within each category, projects are first tiered by maintenance status, then ranked by a blend of stars (40%), 90-day default-branch commits (35%) and recency of the last commit (25%). The maintenance score does not represent final-video quality, model capability, copyright safety or production readiness.
templates.shortlist_note: Shows only core candidates with a verified open license and commits in the last 90 days; restricted-license projects, base models, research benchmarks and adjacent tools are excluded from this table.
templates.toc_note: `★User reference` marks projects provided directly by the user. Models, editors, Skills, CLIs and benchmarks are categorized separately.
templates.detail_intro: Each positioning statement comes from the official README at a pinned commit; not every project was installed and run. Metrics refreshes do not automatically re-audit features or licenses.
templates.rankings_intro: Snapshot: `{as_of}`. This is a ranking of GitHub maintenance metadata, not a video-quality leaderboard. All views tier by maintenance status first.
templates.choose:
- Have footage and need to cut: see editors/workbenches or Skills/MCP.
- From topic and script to finished video: see Agent production and knowledge shorts.
- Motion graphics, product demos and data stories: see Code-to-video.
- Local diffusion generation: see ComfyUI and open models.
- Digital humans/talking heads: see portrait animation and lip sync, and check person consent first.
- Getting properly licensed media: see [CLI comparison](docs/cli-comparison.md).

templates.thanks:
Original curation and scripts in this catalogue use the [MIT]({R}LICENSE) license; linked projects, models, weights, media and fonts follow their own licenses. Source-available, non-commercial, community-model and conditional licenses keep their original boundaries.

Project discovery referenced external indexes such as [Awesome Video Editing](https://github.com/devanasolver/awesome-video-editing); every final entry was verified against its official repository.
templates.records_note: The [change records]({R}record/) keep each entry in the language used at verification time (Chinese), so the source and original wording of every decision stay auditable.
